clues.text: On the desert road to Gaza, Philip met this Ethiopian court official who oversaw Queen Candace's treasury.
Heading home from worship in Jerusalem, he sat in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
Traveling with Philip, he saw water by the road and asked what could prevent him from being baptized.
After the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, this newly baptized traveler went on his way rejoicing.
At the citadel of Susa, Hegai served the king in this role, caring for the young women in the harem.
Through Isaiah, the LORD told this kind of man not to say, "I am but a dry tree."
Through Isaiah, God promised such men who keep His Sabbaths a name better than sons and daughters.
